posts.text:
The Titanic sank on April 15, 1912, killing around 1,500 people. This map breaks the European dead down by home country — and the numbers aren't remotely proportional to population.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Britain's passengers suffered more deaths than any other nation on this map — 223. That figure doesn't even include the crew, who were almost entirely British too and pushed the true toll far higher.
2/ Sweden lost 86 people. Around 113 Swedes had boarded, most as third-class emigrants headed for new lives in America — only 27 of them survived, a death rate far above the ship's overall average.

3/ Finland, then a Grand Duchy inside the Russian Empire, lost about 42 of its roughly 63 passengers — close to a 70% death rate. Nearly all were emigrants in third class, exactly where the evacuation failed hardest.
4/ Ireland's 78 dead were almost entirely third-class passengers who'd boarded at Queenstown, now Cobh, the ship's last port before the Atlantic — many of them leaving Ireland for good.

5/ Austria-Hungary recorded 41 deaths, largely Croatian and Slovenian emigrants in third class. The pattern repeats across the whole map: nationality mattered less than which deck you slept on.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
